stem: Which sentence speculates about the future most naturally?
choices: I'd imagine that most cars will be electric within twenty years.
Most cars are electric in twenty years.
Most cars were electric within twenty years.
I imagine most cars being electric in twenty years ago.
explanation: I'd imagine + will is a natural way to predict.

stem: Which sentence compares past and present correctly?
choices: People used to write letters, whereas now they mostly send messages.
People use to write letters, whereas now they mostly send messages.
People were used to write letters, now they send messages.
People used to writing letters, whereas now messages.
explanation: Used to + verb describes past habits.

stem: Which sentence shows the speaker is fairly sure?
choices: It's highly likely that prices will keep rising.
Prices might possibly perhaps rise.
Prices rising, maybe.
Prices will rise, I don't know.

stem: Which sentence shows the speaker is uncertain?
choices: It might be the case that fewer people will travel by plane.
Fewer people will definitely travel by plane.
It is certain that fewer people travel by plane.
Fewer people must travel by plane.

stem: Question: "What would happen if cars were banned from city centres?" Which answer is grammatically correct?
choices: If cars were banned, the air would be much cleaner.
If cars are banned, the air would be cleaner.
If cars were banned, the air will be cleaner.
If cars banned, the air is cleaner.
explanation: A hypothetical question takes the second conditional.

stem: Which answer gives a balanced view?
choices: There are pros and cons. Online learning is flexible, but it can be isolating for some students.
Online learning is good.
Online learning is bad, very bad.
Online learning, flexible.
explanation: Mention both sides, then you can add your view.

choices: On the whole, young people tend to be more comfortable with technology.
All young people are good at technology.
Young people are always using technology every time.
Technology is young.
explanation: Tend to and on the whole avoid over-generalising.

stem: Which sentence describes a change correctly?
choices: Families have become smaller over the last few decades.
Families became smaller over the last few decades now.
Families are becoming smaller since decades.
Families have became smaller.
explanation: Present perfect for a change up to now.

stem: Which phrase introduces a long-term prediction?
choices: In the long run,
Yesterday,
At the moment,
In the past,
explanation: In the long run refers to the distant future.

stem: Question: "Why are people living longer?" Which answer explains causes well?
choices: Mainly because of better healthcare, but improved diets and safer working conditions have also played a part.
Because they are old.
People live long.
Healthcare.
explanation: Give a main cause and supporting causes.

stem: Which sentence compares two groups correctly?
choices: Older people are generally less likely to shop online than younger people.
Older people are generally less likely shopping online than younger.
Older people less likely to shop online as younger people.
Older people are generally more less likely to shop online.

stem: Which is the most natural way to soften an opinion in Part 3?
choices: I'd say that schools could do more to teach practical skills.
Schools must do more. Everyone knows this.
Schools are wrong.
I am sure 100 per cent schools are bad.
explanation: I'd say and could soften the statement.

stem: Question: "If you could change one thing about your city, what would it be?" Which answer fits?
choices: I'd probably build more parks, because there's very little green space.
I will build more parks.
I build more parks.
I would built more parks.
explanation: Would + base verb answers a hypothetical question.

choices: When I was a child, we would play outside until it got dark.
When I was a child, we will play outside until dark.
When I was a child, we would played outside.
When I am a child, we played outside.
explanation: Would + verb can describe repeated past actions.

stem: Which sentence uses the future continuous naturally?
choices: In ten years, many people will be working from home.
In ten years, many people will working from home.
In ten years, many people are be working from home.
In ten years, many people will be work from home.
explanation: Will be + -ing for an ongoing future situation.

choices: To some extent, yes, but
Absolutely, without any doubt.
No, never.
I totally disagree.
explanation: To some extent signals partial agreement.
